lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Saturday, eight a.m., the kitchen of a flat in Block 208.
**Mum:** The new floor tiles are here! **Octagons** and **squares**. The contractor wants two thousand dollars.
**Dad:** Two thousand? We'll do it **ourselves**. I watched a **video**.
**Kavya:** Dad, you watched **half** a video. At double speed.
**Dad:** The important half.
**Ah Boy:** I'm in charge of the **scissors**! I'll cut everything!
**Mum:** You're in charge of **sweeping**.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is about the corner of the kitchen, where the two walls meet.
**Rex:** Rex. **Right angle**. Exactly **90°**. I've held up this corner since 1987.
**Rex:** Not eighty-nine. Not ninety-one. **Ninety**. Marked with a little **square**, thank you.
**Dad:** Looks **about** ninety to me.
**Rex:** About? ABOUT?! Put the protractor down.
**Rex:** This weekend, every angle in this flat gets **inspected**. No **reason**, no approval.
**Narrator:** All the Right Angles. Episode 13: The Great Kitchen Reno.
**Narrator:** Eight fifteen. Ah Boy has found the scissors anyway.
**Ah Boy:** Small snip, under 90°: **acute**. Exactly 90°: **right**, like Rex. Between 90° and 180°: **obtuse**. More than 180°: **reflex**!
**Dad:** Two cuts from one point on a tile's edge: **52°**, **x**, **73°**. I'll measure x.
**Rex:** Put. The protractor. Down. It says **not drawn to scale**. And angles on a **straight line** add to **180°**.
**Kavya:** x = 180° − 52° − 73° = **55°**, because **angles on a straight line** add to 180°.
**Rex:** An answer, with its **reason**. Approved.
**Ah Boy:** Look, the open scissors make the letter **X**! This angle is **38°**.
**Mum:** Its neighbour is on a straight line with it: 180° − 38° = **142°**.
**Kavya:** The angle **opposite** is **38°** again. **Vertically opposite** angles are equal.
**Ah Boy:** They only touch at the tips. Like me and Kavya in the back seat.
**Mum:** And all four make **360°**: **angles around a point**.
**Dad:** Mine open to **(3x + 10)°** and, opposite, **(5x − 30)°**. Unsolvable!
**Kavya:** Vertically opposite, so **3x + 10 = 5x − 30**. So 2x = 40, and **x = 20**.
**Rex:** They asked for the **angles**: 3 × 20 + 10 = **70°**. The other pair: **110°**.
**Narrator:** Ten a.m. The old tiles are up. Dad snaps two **chalk lines** across the floor.
**Para:** Para. And my wife, Lel. We're **parallel**: same direction, always.
**Lel:** Forty years side by side. Never met. It's the secret of a happy marriage.
**Trevor:** Trevor! **Transversal**! I cross lines! Two at once!
**Kavya:** Trevor crosses Para at **115°**. Lel is parallel, so he crosses her at **exactly the same angle**.
**Rex:** So eight angles, only **two** sizes: **115°**, and 180° − 115° = **65°**.
**Kavya:** Same position at each crossing: **corresponding** angles, **equal**. An **F** shape.
**Priya:** Between the lines, on opposite sides of Trevor: **alternate** angles, **equal**. A **Z**!
**Dad:** Between the lines, on the **same** side: **co-interior**. Also equal. I watched a video.
**Rex:** REJECTED. **Co-interior** angles **add to 180°**: 115° + 65°. A **C** shape.
**Ah Boy:** **F** and **Z** are equal. **C** **C**ompletes 180!
**Priya:** Co-interior with **128°**? 180° − 128° = **52°**, because **co-interior angles add to 180°**!
**Narrator:** Noon. Dad drills a spice shelf into the wall.
**Mr Tan:** Mr Tan, from upstairs. Also, sadly for Kavya, her **maths teacher**.
**Dad:** The brackets are **triangles**. Strong, and their angles add to **180°**. I watched a video.
**Ah Boy:** Every triangle? Even the long thin weird ones? Why?
**Mr Tan:** Draw a line through the top, **parallel** to the base. Para, Lel, would you mind?
**Para:** Delighted. From a respectful distance.
**Lel:** Another parallel line? Oh! Let's name him **Little Lel**.
**Kavya:** The base angles **a** and **b** reappear at the top as **alternate angles**. With **c**, they make a **straight line**.
**Mr Tan:** So **a + b + c = 180°**, for **every** triangle. Even equilateral: **60°** each.
**Mum:** This bracket is **isosceles**: two equal sides, so the two **base angles** are equal. The top angle is **40°**.
**Priya:** Next bracket has a **50°** angle. So: 50°, 50°, **80°**. Done!
**Mr Tan:** Or the 50° is the **apex**: (180° − 50°) ÷ 2 = **65°** each. **Two** answers. Check **both**.
**Mr Tan:** Now the shelf: an **exterior angle** of **117°** = the **sum** of the **interior opposite** angles, **x** and **2x**.
**Mr Tan:** I'd tell you a triangle joke, but it's a bit **acute**.
**Ah Boy:** A cute! Like me!
**Narrator:** Two p.m. Ah Boy makes a kite from a tile box, for kite day at **Marina Barrage**.
**Kitty:** Kitty. A **kite**, darling: two pairs of equal sides **next to each other**, diagonals at **90°**.
**Kavya:** Any quadrilateral's angles add to **360°**: one **diagonal** makes **two triangles**, 2 × 180°.
**Priya:** Mum's tiles are squares, not **rectangles**. Rectangles have two long sides and two short ones.
**Rex:** REJECTED. A **rectangle** just needs **four right angles**. So every square **is** a rectangle.
**Kitty:** And a **rhombus**, a **parallelogram** and a **kite**. Such a show-off.
**Mum:** In a **parallelogram**, opposite angles are **equal** and neighbours add to **180°**: they're **co-interior**.
**Dad:** I cut a tile wrong: **85°**, **110°** and **72°**. What's the fourth angle?
**Mr Tan:** Puzzle! The diagonals **bisect** each other at **90°**, but they **aren't equal**. Name the shape.
**Priya:** Square! Obviously!
**Kavya:** A square's diagonals are **equal**. It's a **rhombus**.
**Narrator:** Four p.m. Mum switches on the **robot vacuum**.
**Roomby:** Roomby. I clean in **polygons**. At every corner, I **turn**. Beep.
**Ah Boy:** Roomby! Do a **regular pentagon**! Five sides!
**Roomby:** Five turns, and I face the way I started: one **full turn**, **360°**. Any polygon, any number of sides. Beep.
**Kavya:** So each turn, the **exterior angle**, is 360° ÷ 5 = **72°**.
**Rex:** And the **interior angle** is 180° − 72° = **108°**. Inside plus outside: a straight line.
**Dad:** A **hexagon** has six sides, so six triangles: 6 × 180° inside! I watched a video.
**Rex:** REJECTED. From **one corner**, a hexagon makes 6 − 2 = **4** triangles: 4 × 180° = **720°**.
**Ah Boy:** Got it! **Minus two, then times one-eighty!**
**Priya:** Regular hexagon: 360 ÷ 6 = **60°** inside. Next!
**Kavya:** That's the **exterior** angle. Inside is 180° − 60° = **120°**. **EX**terior **EX**its first.
**Mr Tan:** Backwards! A regular polygon has interior angles of **160°**. How many sides?
**Kavya:** Exterior first: 180° − 160° = **20°**. Then n = 360 ÷ 20 = **18** sides.
**Roomby:** Eighteen turns? I'm dizzy. Beep. ...Boop.
**Narrator:** Six p.m. At last, the new tiles go down.
**Bea:** Bea! From the honey jar! Your tiles **tessellate**: **no gaps**, **no overlaps**, and the corners at each point make **360°**!
**Kavya:** A regular octagon: exterior **45°**, interior **135°**. And 135° + 135° + 90° = **360°**!
**Bea:** My honeycomb: **3 × 120°**. Triangles: **6 × 60°**. Squares: **4 × 90°**. The only regular polygons that tile alone!
**Ah Boy:** What about **pentagons**, like on my football?
**Kavya:** 3 × 108° = **324°**: a **36°** gap. A fourth makes **432°**: an overlap. Pentagons don't tile.
**Bea:** So a football mixes them: 108° + 120° + 120° = **348°**. Twelve short, so it **curves**!
**Bea:** And symmetry! A regular hexagon has **6** lines of symmetry, and fits onto itself **6** times in a turn: **order 6**.
**Rex:** A regular polygon with **n sides** has **n lines** and **n turns**.
**Mum:** So our octagon tile: **8** lines, **order 8**, and its smallest turn is 360° ÷ 8 = **45°**.
**Mr Tan:** What a **bee-autiful** tessellation.
**Ah Boy:** Bee-autiful! Ha ha! You're so funny, Mr Tan!
**Narrator:** Sunday. Grouting day. Priya has been busy.
**Priya:** I measured **20** triangles. The **exterior angle** always equals the two **interior opposite** angles. **Proved**!
**Mr Tan:** There are **infinitely many** triangles. What about number twenty-one?
**Priya:** ...I'll measure that one too.
**Kavya:** **Proofs** use **letters**, so they cover **every** triangle: angles **a**, **b**, **c** and exterior angle **d**.
**Mr Tan:** Statement, then reason. **c + d = 180°**: **angles on a straight line**.
**Priya:** **a + b + c = 180°**: **angles in a triangle**!
**Kavya:** So **d** and **a + b** both equal **180° − c**. So **d = a + b**, for **every** triangle.
**Rex:** Statements. Reasons. No measuring. **Approved**.
**Mr Tan:** And to **disprove** a claim, one **counterexample** is enough.
**Dad:** Claim: four **equal sides** means it's a **square**. I watched a video.
**Ah Boy:** A **rhombus**! Four equal sides, no right angles.
**Mr Tan:** Parallel lines have so much in common. It's a shame they'll never meet.
**Lel:** How rude. True, but rude.

chapters.title: The kitchen saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits, the kitchen would like to save you some marks.
**Rex:** One. Reasons need **names**: 'alternate angles are equal'. Never 'Z angles'.
**Dad:** Two. **Not drawn to scale**? Don't measure it. Ask me how I know.
**Priya:** Three. **360 ÷ n** is the **exterior** angle. The interior is **180°** minus that.
**Kavya:** Four. Found **x**? Finish the job: work out the angle they asked for, like **3x + 10**.
**Para:** Five. Never **assume** lines are parallel because they look it. Look for the **arrows**.
**Ah Boy:** Six. Isosceles, one angle given? It could be the apex **or** a base angle. Try **both**.
**Narrator:** All the Right Angles will return.
**Narrator:** Monday, seven a.m. The floor is finished.
**Mum:** Octagons, squares, no gaps. It's **perfect**. Except... that last corner.
**Dad:** The corner isn't ninety. It's **91°**. Old HDB walls, lah. I watched a video.
**Rex:** Ninety... **one**?
**Rex:** I need to lie down.
